validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/ATTRIBUTION: The sheet's own current_ref (https://www.petroleum.gov.eg/en/investment/investment-chances/Pages/transporting-marketing.aspx) 404s, confirmed by both the worklist's existing_ref_checks and my own re-check -- a genuine dead link (page removed), not a block. Its gem.wiki page's second harvested citation is that same dead petroleum.gov.eg URL, so the wiki offers nothing further. Its FIRST harvested citation, egyptoil-gas.com's 'Petroleum Ministry to Secure LPG Supply in Winter' (2015-10-18, verified live and independently re-read), DOES corroborate the pipeline's existence: 'During the meeting the progress of the 127km Assiut/Sohag pipeline was reviewed. The project is worth EGP 350m, and will be linked to the Shukeir/Assuit pipeline to transfer LPG to the Sohag filling plant.' This is an Egyptian industry trade-press original report (not GEM-derived, not a wire reprint) and it independently confirms: (1) the pipeline is real and was under active construction as of Oct 2015 (consistent with GEM's StartYear1=2017, i.e. commissioned ~2 years later); (2) it runs Assiut->Sohag and terminates at 'the Sohag filling plant', matching GEM's EndLocation 'Sohag LPG Filling Station'; (3) it is fed by the Red Sea (Ras Shukeir/Ras Gharib)->Asyut LPG trunk system, i.e. it is the final-mile continuation of that corridor, not a standalone/duplicate line. A second, independently-sourced 2020 youm7.com article (cited on sibling rows P7364/roster network, Arabic, verified live, quote: 'تم الانتهاء من القطاع الثانى (خشم الرقبة/أسيوط الجديدة) بتنفيذ خط موازى قطر 12 بوصة بطول 130 كيلو متر ... وتم للخط لتسليم أسيوط وسوهاج بالمعدلات الجديدة من كميات البوتاجاز' = 'the second sector [Khashm El Raqaba/New Asyut] was completed with a parallel 12-inch, 130km line ... and the line now delivers to Asyut and Sohag at the new increased LPG rates') independently corroborates that a real, government-confirmed, actively-upgraded (2600->4000 t/day nationwide) LPG delivery network reaches both Asyut and Sohag -- consistent with GEM's classification (transmission, LPG, operating) though it describes the upstream trunk rather than naming this exact Asyut-Sohag segment by itself. DUPLICATE CHECK vs the 46-row roster: no other row's endpoint is Sohag, so this is not a relabel of P7341/P7363/P7364/P7975 (all of which run Red Sea coast -> Asyut and stop there) -- P7333 is the one downstream continuation onward to Sohag, a distinct physical segment, not a double-count. CAVEATS (see the separate spec concern below and unresolved items): the 2015 source's own length figure (127km) does not match GEM's 114km; the granular endpoint names 'Gahdam' (start) and 'Manfalut' district could not be independently verified in either source found (WebSearch quota was exhausted for this session before a targeted place-name search could be run, and web.archive.org's content-serving path timed out repeatedly for the archived petroleum.gov.eg capture, though its CDX 'available' API confirms a 2025-07-01 snapshot exists at http://web.archive.org/web/20250701184832/https://www.petroleum.gov.eg/en/investment/investment-chances/Pages/transporting-marketing.aspx for a future session to try reading). Fuel=LPG, PipelineType=transmission, and Status=operating are all consistent with both sources and with the rest of the roster's parallel LPG-to-filling-station rows -- no reclassification indicated.

validity.recommendation: Do not silently keep LengthKnown=114km as high-confidence -- flag for a primary-source recheck (an EGPC/PPC/GOGET annual report or the SUMED-adjacent Petroleum Pipelines Co. project list, if accessible) since the only independent source found states 127km, an ~11% conflict.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC: GEM records LengthKnown=114.00 km for this pipeline. The only independently-verifiable source that names this exact segment, egyptoil-gas.com's 2015-10-18 article (verified live, tokens 'Assiut', 'Sohag' and '127km' all present in the retrieved HTML), states 'the progress of the 127km Assiut/Sohag pipeline was reviewed' -- a materially different figure (127 vs 114 km, ~11% longer). This is a single source, and it disagrees with the GEM value rather than confirming it, so per the corroboration standard this cannot be marked high or even a clean medium on the length field specifically: I found no second source giving either 114 or 127km. Two possible explanations, neither confirmable from what I could reach this session: the 2015 article is describing a somewhat different original routing (127km) that was later realigned to 114km when finished in 2017, or the sheet's current 114km figure has some other unverified origin now that its own [ref] cell 404s. Diameter (12in) is not directly attested for THIS segment by either source (the 12in figure in the 2020 youm7 piece is for the separate upstream Khashm El Raqaba-New Asyut sector), so it should also be read as unconfirmed rather than corroborated, though I am not raising it as a standalone concern given no conflicting figure was found for it.

summary: P7333 (Asyut-Sohag LPG Pipeline) is real and correctly classified/attributed (existence + network corroborated by an independent 2015 egyptoil-gas.com article naming the segment directly, plus a 2020 youm7.com article on the same delivery network) -- verdict confirmed (caveat), sheet's own [ref] is a dead link -- but the 2015 source's stated length (127km) conflicts with GEM's recorded 114km (~11%), flagged as an open spec concern; Capacity left blank (no source supports a number).
